summary: Diff adds an eval suite for a new adversarial-review-2 skill: evals.json defines two red-team evals (a Redis session-cache design and a follow-the-sun on-call plan), each with a prompt, expected output, and expectation checklist. It adds the two fixture documents with planted flaws (KEYS-based invalidation, 8GB sizing, timezone coverage gap, untested Krakow team). It also edits adversarial-review/SKILL.md description to route severity-graded or retest requests to adversarial-review-2.

claims.text: evals.json expects reports to flag 200k sessions x 40KB = 8GB equal to free cluster memory.
session-cache-design.md states ~40KB per hash, ~200k sessions, 8GB free, matching the eval expectation.
Invalidation uses KEYS session:*:pricing then DEL on a shared Redis cluster, the planted blocking flaw.
Eval expects timezone gap: Krakow 08:00-20:00 CET = 02:00-14:00 ET, leaving 20:00-02:00 ET uncovered.
On-call plan notes Krakow team joined 6 weeks ago, no prod ships, access still in progress.
adversarial-review SKILL.md now routes severity-graded findings or retest loops to adversarial-review-2.

risks.note: References adversarial-review-2 skill; its SKILL.md is not in this chunk, so existence is unconfirmed.
CET-to-ET 6-hour offset assumed; DST mismatch weeks make it 5 hours, shifting the stated gap.
Files paths are relative (evals/files/...); resolution base directory not shown in chunk.

least_confident: Whether the adversarial-review-2 SKILL.md exists and whether the eval runner resolves the relative files paths, since neither appears in this chunk.
